summary:
Pawstro is a zero-dependency tablet and first-person Helmet Visor HUD web application developed by Team Hibernation Wale Bhalu for the NASA Space Apps 2026 Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map challenge.

What We Developed:
Pawstro provides suited Mars astronauts with a hyper-local (10 by 10 km) tactical navigation console for Jezero Crater. It integrates five toggleable NASA layers including HiRISE/CTX optical imagery, MOLA/HRSC elevation contours, CRISM spectral minerals, steep no-go hazard zones, and THEMIS thermal data, alongside real-time Perseverance MEDA weather and Curiosity RAD radiation telemetry.

How It Addresses the Challenge:
Using an 8-directional A-Star pathfinding engine on a 2D Digital Elevation Model (DEM) cost grid, Pawstro calculates safe walking routes from the habitat to science targets. Routes dynamically adapt to spacesuit limits (maximum slope, distance, and oxygen budget) and optimization modes (Safest, Fastest, Most Science). A real-time 0 to 100 Safety Score, GO/NO-GO badge, Return-to-Base timer, and immersive Visor HUD featuring real Perseverance rover panoramas keep crew safety first.

Why It Matters:
Astronauts on Mars cannot rely on cloud-dependent global maps or fragmented GIS datasets. Pawstro unifies multi-instrument NASA data into a resilient, offline-capable survival tool that turns complex orbital telemetry into actionable, life-saving surface navigation.
details:
PAWSTRO: Tactical Mars EVA Mission Planner and First Person Helmet Visor HUD Challenge: NASA International Space Apps Challenge 2026 | Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map Team: Hibernation Wale Bhalu Mission Crew: Abhinav, Aditi, Harsha, Nikhil Target Site: Jezero Crater Western Delta, Mars (18.4447 N, 77.4508 E, Sol 142)

  1. EXECUTIVE OVERVIEW

When astronauts transition from orbital observation to surface exploration on Mars, global planetary maps are insufficient for day to day survival. Standing on the basin floor of Jezero Crater inside a pressurized spacesuit, an explorer requires immediate, localized intelligence to navigate steep scarps, manage consumable life support reserves, and locate high priority astrobiological samples before nightfall.

Developed by Team Hibernation Wale Bhalu, Pawstro is a localized (10 by 10 kilometer), zero dependency Extravehicular Activity (EVA) mission planning console and first person Helmet Visor Heads Up Display (HUD). Instead of requiring astronauts and flight controllers to cross reference multiple separate geographic information systems, Pawstro unifies NASA optical satellite imagery, topographic elevation contours, orbital spectral mineralogy, surface thermal inertia, radiation dose rates, and local Martian weather into a single, offline capable spacecraft interface. The platform pairs an 8 directional A Star pathfinding engine with an interactive mission communicator, CAPCOM Paw, ensuring that every surface traverse remains strictly within human physiological and hardware safety limits.

  1. SYSTEM FUNCTIONALITY AND TECHNICAL WORKFLOW

Pawstro operates as a dual mode tactical system engineered for the two primary phases of a Martian surface excursion: Pre EVA Tactical Planning (Tablet Console View) and Active Surface Traverse (First Person Helmet Visor HUD Mode).

A. Deep Space Mission Onboarding Upon initialization, operators enter an obsidian black Deep Space Landing Console (#030308) featuring an animated meteor field, live landing site coordinates (18.4447 N, 77.4508 E), the crew manifest plaque, and the floating polar bear astronaut mascot. Operators can transition directly into the main planning console or initiate the 30 second Automated Judge Demo, which loads optimal suit parameters, calculates a complete multi target traverse, and opens science target dossiers in a single action.

B. Five Layer NASA GIS Stack and Split Screen Comparison Engine Within the central viewport, Martian Orange (#ff6a3d) is reserved exclusively for the Jezero Crater map to maximize visual contrast against the surrounding dark avionics panels. Pawstro aligns five toggleable scientific datasets within a unified 700 by 460 orbital coordinate grid:

  1. Photo (Optical): High contrast shaded relief displaying the Neretva Vallis ancient river channel, the Western Delta fan, shaded impact craters (Belva Crater, Kodiak Butte, Santa Cruz), and aeolian regolith ripples across the volcanic Maaz formation floor.
  2. Terrain Height (Topography): Five elevation contour intervals ranging from the 2540 meter basin floor to the 2380 meter delta rim, modeled on MOLA and HRSC Digital Elevation Models.
  3. Minerals (Spectral): MRO CRISM spectral overlays identifying magnesium carbonate lakeshore margin units and iron/magnesium smectite clay and olivine deposits where ancient water interacted with bedrock.
  4. Steep and No Go Zones: Hatched crimson hazard polygons marking cliff scarps exceeding 18 degrees and dense boulder fields that compromise spacesuit stability.
  5. Heat (Thermal): THEMIS thermal inertia anomaly layers that assist crew members in distinguishing consolidated bedrock from unconsolidated dust traps.

Operators can blend overlapping layers using a continuous Opacity Slider (20% to 100%) or engage the Interactive Split Screen Layer Comparison tool. Using a dynamic SVG clipping mask and a cursor tracked vertical divider, users can swipe across Jezero Crater to compare raw optical imagery directly against spectral mineral deposits and topographic hazards. Full viewport controls (Zoom In, Zoom Out, Habitat Center, True North Reset, drag panning, and real time cursor Latitude/Longitude tracking) provide complete spatial awareness.

C. Slope Aware A Star Pathfinding Engine and Reactive Suit Limits At the core of Pawstro is a custom 8 directional A Star pathfinding algorithm operating over a 70 by 46 Digital Elevation Model (DEM) and slope cost grid at a 10 meter cell resolution. Planners can compute routes from Habitat Base (Octavia E. Butler Landing Site) to individual locations (Target A: Wildcat Ridge at 0.8 km; Target B: Kodiak Butte at 1.5 km; Target C: Neretva Delta Fan at 2.3 km) or sequence all targets into an integrated tour. The routing engine supports three optimization modes:

  1. Safest Mode: Applies an exponential cost penalty to terrain incline, directing the astronaut around steep ridges and boulder fields through flat basin corridors.
  2. Fastest Mode: Computes the shortest Euclidean path that remains below the spacesuit's maximum allowable slope threshold.
  3. Most Science Mode: Weights the traversal cost function to route the astronaut through high concentration CRISM carbonate and clay spectral zones, maximizing geological sampling opportunities.

The pathfinding engine is directly coupled to three interactive Spacesuit Limit Sliders: Maximum Slope (5 to 35 degrees), Maximum Distance (1 to 8 km), and Oxygen Reserve (1 to 10 hours). Reducing the Maximum Slope slider dynamically expands the red no go hazard zones on the map and forces the A Star algorithm to compute a wider detour around steep scarps in under 10 milliseconds, simultaneously updating the Elevation Profile Chart, Total Distance, Estimated Walking Time, and Steepest Incline metrics.

D. Real Time Safety Evaluation, Return to Base Timer, and Emergency Abort In alignment with NASA human rating priorities, Pawstro dedicates its lower avionics bay to continuous life support and environmental monitoring:

  1. Route Safety Score (0 to 100) and GO / NO GO Indicator: Continuously evaluates the active route's steepest incline, total distance, and estimated duration against the astronaut's suit limits, alongside Perseverance MEDA weather baselines (minus 12 degrees Celsius, 6 m/s wind speed) and Curiosity RAD surface radiation figures (0.6 uSv/h). If any suit threshold is exceeded, the safety score drops below operational minimums, the status badge transitions from emerald GO to crimson NO GO, and the console outputs the specific parameter violation.
  2. Head Back By Countdown Timer: Combining the current Martian Sol clock (11:05), available oxygen reserve, return walking duration, and local sunset time (17:12), Pawstro calculates the exact turn back deadline required to return to the habitat before nightfall.
  3. Emergency Return to Base (RTB): In the event of a suit anomaly or environmental hazard, engaging the Return to Base control aborts the active science tour, computes a direct low slope A Star escape path back to Habitat Base, and highlights the trajectory in high visibility coral.

E. First Person Helmet Visor HUD with Real Perseverance Rover Panoramas When transitioning from pre mission planning to surface execution, selecting HUD Mode switches Pawstro into a fullscreen, first person Helmet Visor Display. Framed by curved visor glass vignettes and instrumentation brackets, the HUD integrates actual NASA/JPL Caltech Perseverance Rover surface photographs of Jezero Crater for each waypoint (Sol 3 Octavia E. Butler Landing Hazcam panorama, Sol 466 Wildcat Ridge sulfate beds, Sol 63 Kodiak Butte delta foreset strata, and Sol 420 Western Delta scarp). Stepping through waypoints via the Next Waypoint control cross fades the visor background to the corresponding Martian surface photograph while updating the top cardinal compass tape, center target reticle, Slope Ahead warning module, oxygen progress bar, and synchronized Live Visor Mini Map. To guarantee operational resilience in offline environments, an integrated procedural HTML5 Canvas generator synthesizes a 1280 by 720 Martian surface panorama whenever external network connectivity is unavailable.

  1. OPERATIONAL BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT
  2. Cognitive Offloading During High Workload EVA Operations: Suited astronauts operate under physical exertion and restricted visibility. By synthesizing five separate orbital and surface datasets into a single 0 to 100 Safety Score and a clear GO / NO GO indicator, Pawstro reduces cognitive load during time critical surface decisions.
  3. Offline Mission Resilience: Surface exploration tools cannot depend on continuous high bandwidth connectivity. Pawstro packages its entire pathfinding engine, DEM cost grid, SVG cartography, persistent field notes, JSON route exporter, and printable PDF mission briefing generator into a single self contained bundle under 350 KB that executes 100% offline.
  4. Bridging Orbital Remote Sensing and Surface Execution: Pawstro demonstrates a scalable methodology for fusing orbital reconnaissance (HiRISE, MOLA, CRISM, THEMIS) with surface telemetry (Perseverance MEDA, Mastcam Z, Curiosity RAD). This architecture is directly applicable to future lunar Artemis surface traverses, human Mars expeditions, and terrestrial analog field campaigns.
  5. TOOLS, LANGUAGES, AND SOFTWARE ARCHITECTURE

Pawstro was engineered for high performance, cross platform portability, and zero dependency reliability:

  1. Core Technologies: Vanilla HTML5, CSS3 (Custom Properties, CSS Grid, Glassmorphic Backdrop Filters, Keyframe Animations, Print Media Queries), and ES6+ JavaScript.
  2. Cartography and Rendering Engines: Inline Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) utilizing dynamic clip paths, custom hazard hatching, and multi stop radial lighting gradients, paired with HTML5 2D Canvas for real time elevation profile plotting and procedural offline panorama generation.
  3. Algorithms and Local Persistence: Custom 8 directional A Star grid search algorithm over a 70 by 46 DEM and slope matrix; browser LocalStorage API for persistent astronaut field notes and sample collection tracking; Blob and ObjectURL APIs for structured JSON telemetry export.
  4. NASA Datasets Integrated: Mars 2020 HiRISE and CTX orthomosaics (USGS Astrogeology), MOLA and HRSC elevation models, MRO CRISM spectral mineral mappings (Mars Trek), Perseverance Mastcam Z and Hazcam surface imagery, Perseverance MEDA weather logs, and Curiosity RAD radiation baselines.
  5. Automated Verification Suite: Node.js verification environment executing a 14 suite, 132 assertion automated End to End (E2E) test script (test_e2e_full.js) that validates JavaScript compilation, A Star path geometry, slope limit enforcement, and HUD state synchronization.
  6. CREATIVE DESIGN AND HUMAN FACTORS
  7. Intuitive Telemetry Companion (CAPCOM Paw): To make complex planetary data accessible to both mission specialists and public audiences, our compact 96 pixel polar bear astronaut mascot serves as a context aware mission communicator in the corner of the viewport. Selecting science goals, logging rock samples, or breaching suit safety limits triggers immediate, human readable voice bubble updates alongside formal numerical telemetry.
  8. Multi Scale Geological Inspection: Within each Science Target Dossier modal, operators can cycle through a three view Rover POV Carousel (Wide Mastcam Z Outcrop, 2.2x Geological Strata Zoom, and False Color Spectrometer Overlay) and jump directly into the fullscreen Helmet Visor HUD focused on that exact outcrop.
  9. Biomechanical and Environmental Realism: Our team accounted for the physical realities of Martian exploration. Because climbing loose regolith in a pressurized suit exponentially increases metabolic oxygen consumption, our cost grid applies non linear slope penalties. Furthermore, because Martian surface temperatures drop below minus 80 degrees Celsius after sunset, our Return to Base timer cross checks both consumable oxygen hours and the 17:12 local sunset deadline. Finally, because the Perseverance rover does not carry an active radiation detector, we integrated Curiosity RAD surface dose baselines and documented all sample and historical data sources transparently within our technical manual and SOURCES.txt.
